paper.title: Navigating the Unknown: Intent Classification and Out-of-Distribution Detection Using Large Language Models
paper.code: None released: the Anthology page lists no code/software attachment, the PDF has no repository link, and GitHub/web searches (2026-09-26) found none.

clinc150.licence: CC BY 3.0 Unported (repo LICENSE); redistribution permitted with attribution
clinc150.note: Release train = 15,000 = paper Table 1. The 1,000 `oos_test` (far-OOD) queries are not used: Table 1 counts 150 intents / 1,500 test utterances; OOD comes from held-out intents.

banking77.licence: CC BY 4.0 (repo LICENSE); redistribution permitted with attribution
banking77.note: Release train = 10,003 = paper Table 1 (train is not used: zero-shot).

source.excluded: DSTC Finance (not selected for this benchmark) and the in-house BIT3 sets (not public).

frozen.fields: id (<dataset>-test-NNNN = 0-based index in the release test list), text (verbatim), intent (release label)
frozen.selection: First 10 utterances of each intent in release file order (paper Section 3.2: 'In the test splits we limit the utterance per intent number to 10'; which 10 is not stated).
frozen.partitions: Three ID/OOD label partitions, sklearn 1.x train_test_split(sorted(intents), test_size=0.5, random_state=seed), seeds 0/1/2; train part = ID, test part = OOD. CLINC150 75/75 intents (750/750 utterances); BANKING77 38 ID / 39 OOD (380/390). Pairwise ID-set overlap: CLINC150 38/38/45 of 75, BANKING77 20/15/16 of 38.

test_n_resolution: Paper Table 1: CLINC150 test 1,500 (UPL 10), BANKING77 770 (UPL 10) = intents x 10; frozen N equal exactly. OOD/ID sizes follow from the 50/50 label split (Section 4.1). BANKING77 38 ID / 39 OOD: the Table 2 baseline row satisfies ALL F1 76.7 = (380 x 92.7 + 390 x 61.1) / 770 exactly, consistent with 38 ID and 39 OOD intents (39 ID / 38 OOD gives 77.1).

english_verification.metadata: Both datasets are English crowd-sourced (CLINC150, Larson et al. 2019) / English banking customer queries (BANKING77, Casanueva et al. 2020).
english_verification.method: langid 1.1.6 on all 2,270 frozen utterances plus non-ASCII-ratio > 5%; all flags inspected; additionally every frozen utterance of the foreign-word-prone CLINC intents translate, change_language, definition and spelling was read.
english_verification.result: CLINC150: 51 langid flags, BANKING77: 25, all short English queries (e.g. 'define discontent', 'spell aaron', 'I lost my card'). No non-ASCII-ratio flags; only non-ASCII characters are a curly apostrophe and a pound sign. translate utterances mention foreign languages but are English sentences ('how do you say fast in spanish'). No non-English or code-mixed rows; none dropped.

metrics.primary: all_macro_f1: macro-F1 over the partition's ID intents + the OOD class ('fallback'), all test utterances; mean over the 3 partitions.
metrics.reported: id_macro_f1 (macro over ID intents, full test set), ood_f1 (F1 of the OOD class), ood_recall; plus ood_precision, accuracy, all_weighted_f1 and id_macro_f1_id_rows (alternatives for the paper's undefined averaging), ood_auroc from P(fallback) (supplementary).
metrics.definition_gap: The paper names 'total (ALL), OOD and ID macro-F1; OOD recall' (Section 3.1) without formulas. Its reported ALL F1 is often below both ID F1 and OOD F1 (e.g. BANKING77 GPT-4o zero-shot 69.4 / 77.2 / 71.6), which a K+1-class macro or support-weighted F1 with full-test-set ID F1 cannot produce; the ID F1 may be computed on ID-gold rows only (our id_macro_f1_id_rows). Comparisons carry this uncertainty.

paper_numbers_table2_gpt4o_and_baseline._note: Table 2 (p. 14656), 50/50 ID/OOD, average of 3 runs; columns ALL F1 / ID F1 / OOD recall / OOD F1, percent.

deviations: No released code, split or seeds: the 10-per-intent test subset (first 10 in release order) and the three 50/50 ID/OOD label partitions (seeds 0/1/2) are reconstructions; the paper's exact utterances and partitions are unknown, so per-number comparisons carry split variance.
Paper's 'average of 3 runs' is mirrored as the mean over three frozen label partitions (Jev is deterministic, so repeated runs of one partition would be identical).

Zero-shot only: Jev gets the paper's zero-shot prompt (A.3) and intent names; the few-shot and hybrid methods use train utterances and a fine-tuned front end and are reported as paper reference points, not reproduced.

Tool calling is replaced by one Jev choice question (ID intents + 'fallback'); the A.3 closing line about tool calling is replaced by a sentence naming the state field. Criterion text per intent = its name with underscores as spaces.
Metric averaging undefined in the paper (see metrics.definition_gap); primary uses the standard K+1 macro-F1 definition.
